description:
Project Overview

This PhD project, supervised by Dr S Romero-Vargas Castrillon, focuses on molecular engineering of water treatment membranes using computational methods and machine learning.

Research Focus

  • Water Scarcity: Developing membranes for unconventional water treatment
  • Molecular Simulation: Using molecular dynamics to understand transport mechanisms
  • Machine Learning: Using ML for materials discovery
  • Membrane Design: Rational design of selective, water-permeable membranes
  • Contaminant Removal: Removing small charge-neutral contaminants

Funding & Benefits

  • Tuition Fees: Potential coverage for UK students for 3.5-4 years
  • Stipend: Competitive funding may be available for 3.5-4 years
  • Research Costs: Access to computational facilities
  • Training: Training in molecular simulation and machine learning

Eligibility Criteria

  • Undergraduate degree at 2:1 or above (preferably supported by MSc)
  • Field: Chemical engineering, mechanical engineering, chemistry, physics, materials science, or cognate field
  • Strong background in mathematics and physics
  • Interest in molecular simulation
  • Prior research experience in modelling and simulation (highly desirable)
  • Residency: UK applicants may be supported for competitive studentships

Application Process

  1. Contact supervisor
  2. Discuss research interests
  3. Submit application through Degree Finder
  4. Provide academic documents
  5. Funding competition
  6. Award notification
